note: Hand-curated. Every fact comes from the scheme's official page. 'next' is filled in only once the official page announces the dates; 'rolling' marks schemes whose official page says they take applications all year. collectors/programs-check.mjs re-reads each 'check_url' daily (except entries with check.auto false) and sets 'check.seen' when the dates on that page change; a person then reviews the entry and copies 'check.seen' into 'check.reviewed'. Left out until their official pages can be read: NIDHI-EIR (guidelines only as a PDF), the Atal New India Challenge (no current call on aim.gov.in), MeitY's TIDE 2.0 and SAMRIDH (script-drawn pages) and Startup Karnataka's Elevate (site did not load).

items.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme
items.summary: Up to ₹20 lakh as a grant to prove a concept or build a prototype, and up to ₹50 lakh as debt for market entry, given through selected incubators.
items.who: A startup recognised by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years before it applies. The full eligibility rules are on the scheme's site.
items.amount: Grant of up to ₹20 lakh for proof of concept, prototype development or product trials, paid in milestone-based instalments. Up to ₹50 lakh as debt or convertible debentures for market entry, commercialisation or scaling up.
items.format: Apply on the Seed Fund portal to one or more of the scheme's incubators
items.usual: Applications are open all year: startups apply on the portal and the chosen incubators review them.

check.reason: The Seed Fund portal is drawn by a script and shows no text to automated readers, so WILSY does not check it daily.

items.name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG)
items.summary: BIRAC's flagship grant for young biotech startups and researchers: up to ₹50 lakh over 18 months to turn an idea into a proof of concept.
items.who: Startups, companies and individual researchers with a biotechnology idea that could be commercialised. The guidelines on the BIRAC site set out who qualifies.
items.amount: Up to ₹50 lakh as grant-in-aid, for a project of up to 18 months.
items.format: Apply online on the BIRAC portal when a call is open; BIG Partners across India mentor and monitor the grantees
items.usual: BIRAC says calls are announced twice a year, on 1 January and 1 July, and stay open for about 45 days. Recent calls have not always kept to that calendar, so watch BIRAC's calls for proposals page.

items.name: NIDHI-PRAYAS
items.summary: Up to ₹10 lakh for students and young innovators to turn a technology idea into a working prototype, with lab space and mentoring at a PRAYAS centre.
items.who: Students, researchers, innovators, entrepreneurs and startups, in any sector. You apply through a NIDHI-PRAYAS centre at a selected incubator.
items.amount: Up to ₹10 lakh per innovator or startup, plus access to the incubator's facilities, fabrication labs and mentors.
items.format: Apply to a NIDHI-PRAYAS centre (at selected technology business incubators); the list of centres is on the NIDHI site
items.usual: Each PRAYAS centre runs its own calls. Check the centres near you, or the NIDHI-PRAYAS website, for open calls.
items.last_edition: Run by DST with SINE, IIT Bombay, as the programme's management unit.

items.name: Kerala Startup Mission grants
items.organizer: Kerala Startup Mission, Government of Kerala
items.summary: Kerala's ladder of non-repayable grants, from an idea grant of up to ₹3 lakh to a scale-up grant of up to ₹15 lakh, with a larger productisation grant for women-led and transgender-led startups.
items.who: Innovators and startups in Kerala, with a focus on first-time founders, student innovators and women-led startups. Each grant's page on the KSUM site says who qualifies.
items.amount: Idea Grant up to ₹3 lakh; Productisation Grant up to ₹7 lakh; Women / Transgender Productisation Grant up to ₹12 lakh; Market Acceleration Grant up to ₹10 lakh; Scaleup Grant up to ₹15 lakh. Grants don't have to be repaid.
items.format: Apply online on the Kerala Startup Mission site, grant by grant
items.usual: KSUM lists these grants as open for applications on its early-stage funding page.
items.last_edition: KSUM also offers seed loans and patent reimbursement, listed on the same page.
